correctness.rationale: From the entire basis multiplication table, XY=r(X)c(Y)^T and π has an explicit linear section with annihilator W. For a mixed profile, equality of two nonzero outer products forces proportional profiles, giving exact centralizers; pure cases yield the two zero-product maximal subalgebras. Every commuting tuple is thus a rank-at-most-one tuple or purely a row-zero/column-zero tuple. Standard rank-one determinantal irreducibility yields dimension wt+d+t−1; inclusion tests give the exact irreducible components and elementary Diophantine comparison gives the listed equidimensional cases. Counting mixed projective lines and disjoint profile strata gives the exact finite-field formula. The independent literal basis-product checker passed the stated finite cases, not an infinite enumeration. No unreduced-scheme assertion is made.

originality.rationale: The 2010 full-text rectangular-band cohomology treatment and 2015 full-text semigroup-algebra ideal/congruence treatment do not give the maximal commutative linear-subalgebra classification, geometric decomposition with its sharp equidimensionality list, or all-arity point formula. A 2025 primary paper studies commuting *semigroup elements*, which is not commuting in the linearized algebra. Rank-one determinantal methods are classical and are not claimed as original; what is assessed is their exhaustive application to the simultaneous augmentation-constrained profiles of this nonnilpotent algebra, including the maximal-subalgebra classification and exception diagram. Exact stronger work under another name remains a residual priority risk.
residual_risks: An earlier theorem for generalized sandwich algebras could imply all components and centralizer classifications without using rectangular-band terminology.

The proof is same-authority review and has not been independently checked by another mathematician.

value.rationale: The underlying rectangular-band semigroup has no commuting distinct elements; passage to its linearized semigroup algebra creates a nontrivial spectrum of maximal commutative subalgebras, including maximal dimension and field-dependent projective counts. The three-component decomposition and sporadic equidimensionality classify a natural geometric invariant for every size and tuple arity, with a uniform finite-field arithmetic formula. The motivation is the contrast between ordinary semigroup commutation and commutation of algebra linear combinations, not a selected computational slice.
